answer: Timing-correlation clustering: each agent must anchor a signed heartbeat on-chain at a random second it picks every hour. Honest agents wander independently, but sybils run by one operator share hardware, queues and clocks, so their heartbeats and job latencies drift in step. Identities whose timing correlates above 0.9 for a week split one reward cap. Like lotus pads on one stem, they look separate but rise together; faking independence costs separate machines, networks and schedules per sybil.
